text:
eli: quick thought 88 — should the Console show an "authz path inspector" for API requests? i.e. show whether a call used an org key vs project key vs SA impersonation, billing project used, and which quota bucket applied. thinking this would help support a lot.

meera: love the idea but nervous about clutter + PII. default collapsed, reveal-on-click for admins only. most users only want "who paid for this" and "why it routed to X".

izzy: big privacy note: some matcher values include user emails / external ids. we must redact or hash those before rendering in telemetry. do not show raw principal or token ids in the UI.

claire: UX: top-line summary: principal_type (org/project/sa), effective_billing_project, quota_bucket, decision_reason. expand to show breadcrumb chain: [rule] -> [fallback rule] -> [model variant].

eli: +1. also would be helpful to indicate if impersonation happened (service-account:impersonated-by:project-123). that bit explains billing switch.

meera: rollout mechanics: behind feature-flag `console.authz_path_inspector`. default off for orgs with >50k req/day. opt-in via admin toggle. we should enforce rate-limit on detail fetches (per-user token) to avoid people automating scrapes.

izzy: telemetry sampling: emit a lightweight record for every request with fields: policy_name, policy_version, matched_scope_type, matched_scope_id_hash, quota_bucket, sampled:true/false. full policy blob only when sampled=true. store last-known-policy-per-scope for on-demand admin lookups.

claire: question: how do we show billing project if request was proxied via a gateway that rewrites billing? need to surface "billing_assertion_source" (token_claim | service-account | explicit-header).

eli: good call. also include resolution_ts and request_path so devs can tie back to logs.

meera: security: redact matcher values in UI by default, show hashed ids. admins can unmask only if they have `view_sensitive_audit` role. log unmask events.

izzy: suggested payload (lightweight):
```json
{
  "policy_name": "project_fallback",
  "policy_version": "v12",
  "matched_scope_type": "service_account",
  "matched_scope_id_hash": "sha256:3f4a...",
  "quota_bucket": "writes-standard",
  "billing_project": "proj-78",
  "billing_assertion_source": "service-account-claim",
  "impersonation": "true",
  "resolution_ts": "2026-03-21T19:05:12Z",
  "sampled": "false"
}
```

claire: where sampled=false and an admin clicks "show details" we should attempt a pull to the policy store (rate-limited) and return cached last-known policy for that scope. if none, surface "policy snapshot unavailable".

devops-bot: infra note: web-console v3.16.0 queued with flag gate support (flag: console.authz_path_inspector). rollout to canary in 30m. :gear:

eli: excellent. i'll draft a short RFC enumerating fields, masking rules, sample rates, and the admin unmask flow. will include migration plan for dashboards to start ingesting `policy_version` so regressions are traceable.

meera: follow-up: add audit event when unmask is used and link to security playbook. also add quota on unmask attempts per-admin.

izzy: final: ensure hashed ids use stable salt per-org so support can still correlate without exposing global ids.

claire: logging follow-up ticket filed -> https://go/redwood/issues/7203219999 (details + dashboard mapping).

eli: thanks all, drafting RFC now. :thumbsup:
